findings.reason: a worker dispatched on this section would be fenced out of the only file holding the defect, and an auditor cannot reconcile the stated resolver with the landing it cites.
findings.text: §18's Why states "The tier resolver (`recovery_repair_dispatch._sweep_review_tier` through `reckon/review_tiers.py`) measures the change from the commits a run cites" and its write paths at line 174 name `reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py`, `reckon/review_tiers.py` and `reckon/crew/obligations.py`, yet commit `6aa28c43e7` (merged as the cited `ee7fb80c4e`) added `_with_the_runs_whole_change` in `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py` — `_sweep_review_tier` only calls `promotion._run_review_tier`, so the section points at the caller and the leaf while the mechanism named is the shared core in a file its write paths exclude

findings.reason: the followup's range is the instruction a coordinator executes, so it must be rewritten to cover the sections the declarations open.
findings.text: the single open followup is titled "Land §2, then build §3 to §11" while `plan-section-declarations` at line 23 now declares s12–s17 implementable and s18 done, so the plan's own chain stops six buildable sections short and can be resolved with s12–s17 unbuilt

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — commit `ee7fb80c4e` resolves in `/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon` as "Merge the review tier measured over a run's whole change" (its fix commit `6aa28c43e7` introduces `_with_the_runs_whole_change`), `reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:2090` defines `_sweep_review_tier`, and the cited run and commits are ids the section states rather than hrefs.
rubric_items.done_when: pass for the changed unit — §18 states each new test fails at the base revision, and re-running `tests/test_a_review_tier_reads_the_runs_whole_change.py` with the whole-change scope replaced by the cited commits alone fails `test_citing_only_the_docs_commit_still_owes_the_change_its_review` (`assert 'none' != 'none'`), so its control fires; the earlier, unanswered done_when findings on §13/§14/§16 belong to unchanged units and are not re-raised.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §18's evidence is a durable landing comment carrying commit `ee7fb80c4e` and the all_debug arm counts, both openable after the run, and no node-local or scratch path is cited.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §18's heading and comment name the mechanism ("the whole change, not the commits it cites") with no plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §18 names the tier resolver and the files it lives in as `recovery_repair_dispatch._sweep_review_tier` through `reckon/review_tiers.py`, but the defect its own landing evidence repaired sat in `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py`, which §18's write paths do not list.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §18's done-when delivers one verdict (the tier resolves from the whole base-to-head change, docs-only change still resolves to none); its third criterion, that no obligation offers `crew complete` for a run owing a review with none stored, is a consequence of the corrected tier rather than a second deliverable, and `reckon/crew/obligations.py:2651` offers that remedy only in the `review_tiers.NONE` branch.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the single open followup at line 179 still titles its build range "§3 to §11" while `plan-section-declarations` now carries s3–s17 implementable and s18 done, so the chain a coordinator follows ends before seven of the plan's sections.
